chunks: If you stay in Medina for three days, fast on Wednesday and pray on Wednesday night at the Pillar of Repentance, which is the pillar of Abū Lubābah where he tied himself, and remain there on Wednesday. Then on Thursday night go to the pillar next to it near the station of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, remain there through your night and day, and fast on Thursday. Then go to the pillar next to the station of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and his place of prayer on Friday night, pray there through your night and day, and fast on Friday. If you are able not to speak during these days except what is necessary, not to leave the mosque except for a need, and not to sleep by night or day except a little, then do so. Praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on Friday, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, then ask for your need, then say:

O Allah, whatever need I may have with You, whether I have begun seeking and pursuing it or have not begun, whether I have asked You for it or have not asked You for it, I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy, concerning the fulfillment of my needs, the small of them and the great of them.

key_terms.أُسْطُوَانَةِ التَّوْبَةِ: the Pillar of Repentance where worship is performed on Wednesday night
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: sawm (fasting) observed on the specified days in al-Madīnah
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: opening invocation addressed to Allah in supplication
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Medina, the setting of this devotional practice
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, from which one should not leave except for a need
key_terms.بِنَبِيِّكَ مُحَمَّدٍ: through Your Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, expressing tawassul in the supplication
key_terms.حَاجَتَكَ: one's need that is to be asked from Allah
key_terms.نَبِيِّ الرَّحْمَةِ: the Prophet of Mercy, a description of the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله in the du'a

ai.seo_question: What devotional practice is recommended in Medina involving fasting, prayer at the pillars, and supplication through the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This report describes a devotional practice in al-Madīnah combining sawm (fasting), salat (prayer), seclusion in the mosque, restraint in speech, and du'a (supplication) at specific pillars near the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. It culminates in a supplication seeking the fulfillment of all needs through turning to Allah by means of the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, the Prophet of Mercy.
